column3: BSB follows the critical text with “our God” and no “honor”; the Textus Receptus has “honor” and “to the Lord our God.” “Belong to” is added.
“That was poured out by her hand” recasts “out of her hand.”
Close to the Greek.
Close to the Greek.
“All you who serve Him” renders “all His servants”; “alike” is added.
BSB follows the critical text with “the Lord our God.” “Reigns” renders the aorist ἐβασίλευσεν (“has begun to reign”).
Close to the Greek.
BSB ends the quotation before the last sentence and adds “she wears.”
“The angel told me to write” recasts “he says to me: Write.”
“Rely on” renders ἐχόντων (“have”).
“There before me was” renders “behold”; “its rider is called” renders “the one sitting on it [is] called.”
BSB has no “names written and” (ὀνόματα); “He has a name written on Him” renders “having … a name written.”
Close to the Greek.
“The armies of heaven” renders “the armies which [are] in heaven.”
BSB has no “two-edged” (δίστομος). “Rule” renders ποιμανεῖ; “iron scepter” renders “rod of iron.”
Close to the Greek.
BSB follows the critical text with “the great supper of God.” “Overhead” renders μεσουρανήματι.
“Of horses and riders” recasts “flesh of horses and of those sitting on them.”
Close to the Greek.
“Along with” and “on its behalf” recast “with him” and “before him”; “both the beast and the false prophet” renders “the two.”
“Gorged themselves” renders ἐχορτάσθησαν (“were filled”).
